text:
maya: Quick sync — we need to lock the API surface decisions for tool-calling + structured output before the docs freeze next sprint. Customers (healthcare + fintech) pushing for typed tool results and stable embeddings API.

samir: +1. What's non-negotiable vs nice-to-have for the first ship?

maya: Non-negotiable: function calling shape (name + args JSON), stable structured-output schema for single-step transforms, and embeddings interface parity with current beta. Nice-to-have: typed SDK helpers, first-class rerank combinator in SDK.

olga: For function calling shape, can we commit to: {"name": "string", "arguments": <opaque JSON>} and then add a typed wrapper in TS/py later? Avoid nested schema versioning pain.

ben: That shape works, but customers want examples of typed bindings. Proposal: release unopinionated JSON shape in API v1, ship TS types in SDK v1.1 with a small opt-in converter util.

jen: Docs ask: we need 3 canonical examples per language — simple tool call, tool call with streaming, and structured-output validation. Who owns examples?

prashant: I'll take Python examples if Ben owns TS. We should keep example PRs tiny. Also propose a changelog note: "API: structured output + function_call shape added" with migration guide.

maya: Launch criteria suggestion: (1) API spec published and stable in prod (2) Python and TS SDKs implement basic helpers + types (3) three worked examples + a short migration doc (4) E2E smoke tests and perf sanity (latency/regressions). Thoughts?

samir: Add: docs lint pass and examples runnable via GH Codespaces/colab. That reduces friction for integrators.

olga: On types: for TS we should expose both a loose JSON type and a generic typed helper: type ToolResult<T> = {name: string; arguments: T}. For Python, provide dataclass + runtime validator util (pydantic optional). Keep validators optional to avoid hard dep.

ben: Agree. For changelog we should call out breaking risks: if customers relied on previous unstructured responses, they may need to opt-in to function_call behavior. We should add an opt-in header or param for the rollout.

maya: Good point. Plan: opt-in by default in beta orgs, opt-out for current prod orgs for 6 weeks. ops to add header: X-Redwood-Function-Calling: beta. Can eng-infra help? @prashant can you loop infra?

prashant: I'll ping eng-infra today. Also will add basic smoke tests: tool-call roundtrip + structured-output validator.

jen: Docs tasks: I'll draft the migration guide and three examples. Need final API shape by EOD Thu to hit next sprint.

ben: ETA for TS helper PR: next Tue. I'll include typed examples and a small utility to coerce args into typed shapes.

olga: Python PR ETA: Wed. Will include dataclass + quick validator example without pydantic, and optional pydantic snippet in extra section.

maya: Ok, action items: jen (docs + migration guide) due Thu EOD; ben (TS examples + helper) Tue; olga (py examples + validator) Wed; prashant (infra smoke tests + rollout header) Thu. Samir will own release checklist & gating. I'll schedule a 30m sync Thu morning to sign off.

samir: I'll prepare the gate checklist: API spec diff, example smoke tests, SDK unit tests, docs smoke, and perf numbers.

docs-bot: Reminder: add a "docs freeze" label on the repo once API spec is approved.

maya: Thanks — small, incremental rollout recommended. We'll revisit rerank combinator for the following milestone.

ben: One tiny note for the changelog: include example curl with header: `curl -H "X-Redwood-Function-Calling: beta" ...`

jen: Copy that. I'll draft first pass and ping for review.

maya: Closing — thanks all. If anyone finds a major blocker, mention it in this thread or ping me directly. :thumbsup:
